key_insight: SIM-PINN combines projection-based segregation, iteration, and multi-stage training to reduce constraint coupling and spectral bias in incompressible flow simulation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a mesh-free route to more accurate and better-converged incompressible Navier–Stokes solutions.
method: Decouple Navier–Stokes into linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations solved by dedicated neural networks.
Couple velocity and pressure through projection-based inner iterations.
Use successive momentum-network stages to refine velocity at targeted frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence and accuracy on steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flows, without numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Computational cost and scalability remain unclear because the abstract does not quantify the overhead of iterative, multi-network training.
paper_title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
